notes: Nill Download Manager 2.0.8 is a reliability release — a second full audit of the engine, the app and the browser extension, fixed end to end. A browser download can no longer be stranded if the browser restarts its extension worker mid-handoff: the hand-off state is stored, and the browser copy is released or kept exactly once. A server that holds a connection open forever can no longer wedge a download — stalled transfers settle within seconds, and Pause, Cancel and Delete always complete. Resuming against a server that refuses the old position no longer truncates the bytes already on disk; a merge finished just as the app closed is adopted on the next start instead of being downloaded again; and deleting a download removes only its own recorded file, never another file that merely matches in size. The speed limiter now holds from the first byte and follows changes within about two seconds, and multi-part video downloads account their size correctly instead of failing a perfect file at the final check. Refresh download address works the way it should: point a dead link at a fresh address for the same file and the download continues from its saved progress — a different file starts over. On Windows 7 and 8 the video engine fetches the last supported yt-dlp build together with a working ffmpeg, and the extension's fast video detection works on older browsers again. The progress dialog gains per-connection states, independent completion options and a working Cancel, and the extension now updates with the app, asking for one browser restart after an update and then staying silent. 2.0.8 is a required update for older versions.
